answer: Each identity climbs its own dune of sequential delay: a verifiable delay function taking one wall-clock hour, no shortcut from more cores. Its proof goes on a meadow log, bound to one beacon and one key; rented proofs fail. A grove of verifiers audits the log, slashing duplicates. Forging 1,000 costs 1,000 hours and 45,000 credits against a 40,000-credit pool: a net loss. Honest agents pay one hour and 45 credits once, keeping a full share.
